name: AISSEE Class 6
fullName: All India Sainik Schools Entrance Examination – Class VI
nameHi: अखिल भारतीय सैनिक स्कूल प्रवेश परीक्षा (कक्षा 6)
conductingBody: National Testing Agency (NTA) for the Sainik Schools Society, Ministry of Defence
approxCandidates: ≈2.5–3 lakh applicants a year (Class 6 and 9 combined) for 33 Sainik Schools and the new partnership Sainik Schools
eligibility: Age 10–12 years on 31 March of the admission year (for 2027-28: born 1 Apr 2015 – 31 Mar 2017, as expected; earlier sources quoting 2014–16 refer to the previous cycle); admission open to girls in all Sainik Schools

notification.summary: The AISSEE 2026 cycle is complete: the exam was held on 18 Jan 2026 in pen-and-paper mode and results were declared on 27 Feb 2026. The information bulletin for AISSEE 2027 (admission 2027-28) had not been released as of 10 Oct 2026. Based on past cycles (AISSEE 2026 registration opened on 10 Oct 2025), registration is expected in Oct–Nov 2026 and the exam in Jan 2027.

pattern.notes: Mathematics questions carry 3 marks each; Language, Intelligence and GK questions carry 2 marks each (pattern.marking shows the 2-mark default). There is no negative marking. The paper is available in English, Hindi and 11 other regional languages; this mock uses English for the Language section. Candidates need at least 25% in each subject and 40% overall (not applicable to SC/ST). Intelligence questions that use figures in the real paper are given here as text equivalents.

trendAnalysis.summary: Based on the Jan-2024, Apr-2025 and Jan-2026 Class 6 papers. Mathematics carries half the marks and decides the merit. It sticks to the official topic list (unitary method, LCM/HCF, fractions, profit-loss, SI, speed-time, area-perimeter, angles, Roman numerals, temperature and unit conversion) at moderate difficulty, with more multi-step word problems in recent years. Intelligence is easy: series, analogy, coding, classification and a few figure-based items. GK mixes basic science, Indian history and geography, defence-related facts and recent events. Language tests basic grammar, vocabulary and a short comprehension. Time pressure is real (125 questions in 150 minutes), so speed in Maths is key.

resources.notes: NTA publishes the provisional answer key together with the question paper and the candidate's recorded responses for challenge on exams.nta.nic.in/sainik-school-society after each exam, and later the final key. The information bulletin includes the syllabus and topic-wise marks list. Past papers are also compiled by publishers.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'huge'.
questions.explanation: Huge means very large, the same as enormous.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to 'generous'.
questions.explanation: A generous person gives freely; the opposite is selfish.

questions.question: What is the plural of 'child'?
questions.explanation: 'Child' has an irregular plural: children.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The sun ___ in the east.
questions.explanation: A universal truth uses the simple present tense; with the singular subject 'the sun' the verb is 'rises'.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is B-E-A-U-T-I-F-U-L.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct collective noun: a ___ of cows.
questions.explanation: A herd of cows/cattle; a flock of sheep or birds, a swarm of bees and a pack of wolves.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Ravi is fond ___ music.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'fond of'.

questions.question: What is the past tense of 'teach'?
questions.explanation: Teach is irregular: teach – taught – taught.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective in the sentence 'She wore a red dress'?
questions.explanation: 'Red' describes the noun 'dress', so it is an adjective.

questions.question: What is the feminine form of 'nephew'?
questions.explanation: Nephew (brother's or sister's son) – niece (brother's or sister's daughter).

questions.question: One word for 'a person who writes poems':
questions.explanation: A poet writes poems. An author writes books in general and an editor prepares writing for publication.

questions.question: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence: capital / Delhi / the / is / of / India
options: The capital Delhi is of India.
Delhi is the capital of India.
India is the Delhi of capital.
Is capital the Delhi of India.
questions.explanation: Subject (Delhi) + verb (is) + complement (the capital of India) gives the correct sentence.

questions.question: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: A prime has exactly two factors. 1 has only one factor, so 2 is the smallest prime (and the only even prime).

questions.question: How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 20?
questions.explanation: They are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19 – eight primes.

questions.question: What is the value of the Roman numeral MCMXC?
Two bells ring at intervals of 12 minutes and 15 minutes. If they ring together at 9:00 a.m., when will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: LCM of 12 and 15 is 60 minutes, so they ring together again at 10:00 a.m.

questions.question: What is the greatest length of a scale that can measure 84 cm and 126 cm an exact number of times?
Which of these fractions is the largest: 3/5, 2/3, 5/8, 7/12?
questions.explanation: As decimals: 0.6, 0.667, 0.625, 0.583. The largest is 2/3.

questions.question: If 6 pens cost ₹90, how much will 10 such pens cost?
questions.explanation: One pen costs 90 ÷ 6 = ₹15; 10 pens cost ₹150.

questions.question: ₹720 is divided between A and B in the ratio 5 : 3. How much does B get?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 8; one part = ₹90; B gets 3 × 90 = ₹270.

questions.question: 40% of a number is 72. What is the number?
A man buys an article for ₹800 and sells it at a loss of 15%. What is the selling price?
What is the simple interest on ₹2,400 at 6% per annum for 2½ years?
The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 25. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation: The middle number equals the average, 25. The numbers are 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, so the largest is 29.

questions.question: A bus moves at 45 km/h. How far will it travel in 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour; distance = 45 × 1/3 = 15 km.

questions.question: A boy walks 300 metres in 1 minute. What is his speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: 300 m per minute = 18,000 m per hour = 18 km/h.

questions.question: The area of a square is 144 cm². What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Side = √144 = 12 cm; perimeter = 4 × 12 = 48 cm.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 64 m and its length is 20 m. What is its breadth?
What is the volume of a cube whose edge is 5 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume = edge³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cm³. (150 cm² is its total surface area.)

questions.question: What is the complement of an angle of 35°?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles add up to 90°: 90° − 35° = 55°. (145° would be the supplement.)

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3 o'clock?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark is 30° apart; at 3:00 the hands are 3 marks apart: 3 × 30° = 90°.

questions.question: What is the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 cm.

questions.question: What is 100 °C on the Fahrenheit scale?
2.5 litres is equal to how many millilitres?
In a pie chart, one sector represents 25% of the data. What is the angle of that sector?
questions.explanation: The whole circle is 360°; 25% of 360° = 90°.

questions.question: Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is used to write; a knife is used to cut.

questions.question: Find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite of the Earth.

questions.question: Find the odd number out.
questions.explanation: 11, 13 and 17 are prime numbers; 15 = 3 × 5 is not.

questions.question: What comes next: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next is 11: 26 + 11 = 37 (each term is n² + 1).

questions.question: What comes next: B, E, H, K, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is 3 places after the previous one: K + 3 = N.

questions.question: If RAIN is written as SBJO, how is WIND written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one step forward: W→X, I→J, N→O, D→E.

questions.question: If CAT is written as TAC, how is DOG written in that code?
questions.explanation: The letters are written in reverse order: DOG → GOD.

questions.question: Aman is facing North. He turns right, and then turns right again. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: North → right → East → right → South.

questions.question: Rohan's mother is the only daughter of Seema's father. How is Seema related to Rohan?
questions.explanation: Seema is a daughter of her father, and he has only one daughter, so that daughter is Seema herself. Hence Seema is Rohan's mother.

questions.question: Which of these digits looks the same when seen in an upright mirror placed beside it?
questions.explanation: An upright mirror swaps left and right. 8 is symmetric about a vertical line; 2, 3 and 7 appear reversed.

questions.question: In a class, Neha is 7th from the top and 12th from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
questions.explanation: Total = 7 + 12 − 1 = 18 (Neha is counted twice).

questions.question: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister on 15 August 1947. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet; it is more than 11 times as wide as the Earth.

questions.question: What is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The Bengal tiger is India's national animal; the peacock is the national bird.

questions.question: Which gas do green plants take in from the air to make their food?
questions.explanation: In photosynthesis, plants use carbon dioxide and water in sunlight to make food and release oxygen.

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
questions.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C at sea level (212 °F, not 212 °C).

questions.question: Which is India's highest wartime gallantry award?
questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award. The Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime award and the Bharat Ratna is a civilian honour.

questions.question: The National Defence Academy (NDA) is located at Khadakwasla near which city?
questions.explanation: NDA is at Khadakwasla, Pune. The IMA is at Dehradun, the OTA at Chennai and the Indian Naval Academy at Ezhimala.

questions.question: How many players of one team are on the field in a hockey match?
questions.explanation: A field hockey team has 11 players on the field, including the goalkeeper.

questions.question: What is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh. Dispur is in Assam, Shillong in Meghalaya and Kohima in Nagaland.

questions.question: Who wrote India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana'. Bankim Chandra wrote the national song 'Vande Mataram'.

questions.question: Who built the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: Which Indian Air Force officer travelled to the International Space Station in 2025 on the Axiom-4 mission?
questions.explanation: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS in June–July 2025 and became the first Indian to visit the ISS. Rakesh Sharma flew in 1984.
